title: Exclusive public lottery licence (New South Wales)
summary: The Public Lotteries Act 1996 (NSW) lets the Minister grant an exclusive operator licence, during which no other operator licence may be granted.
direction_rationale: An exclusive licence keeps all other operators out.

verified.notes: An existing setting: no dates. Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of January 2023 (not itself official); a later change would not show.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 17 November 2026 (phase 6 of the levers re-evaluation, batch 1) from the law quoted. Not yet checked: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: An operator licence for public lotteries may be granted as an exclusive licence, and no other operator licence may then be granted during its exclusivity period (keno aside). A statutory exclusive right to run lotteries.

marks.reason: No other lottery operator may be licensed during the exclusivity period.
The exclusive operator faces no rival in its market.

assessment.confidence_note: The Act allows exclusivity; whether the current licence is exclusive, and to when, is not quoted here.
